title: One regulatory search angle's output (wave 1)
description: What ONE angle retrieved, as a 2-D coverage grid plus the instruments it admitted. Written to search/<angle_id>.yaml — one file per search child.

cell.description: ONE (group, source) pair of the 2-D coverage grid. Both keys are required because the grid is two-dimensional: a cell keyed on the source alone cannot say which vocabulary reached it, and a missing pair then passes as covered.

group_id.description: A group the map minted. Not a term — the id.

source_id.description: A registry source id the map recorded ACTIVE.

queries.description: Every request VERBATIM as issued, and for a structured source the filter expression too. A paraphrase cannot be re-run, and this type's queries are identifier resolutions whose exact form decides what comes back — the Cellar `Accept` pair is part of the request, not decoration.

timestamp.description: When this cell was worked. Per-cell, because a wave can span a rate-limit window.

status.description: What HAPPENED. `gated` is not `unreachable`: a source that answered and then demanded a key completed the fetch and refused it. `not-attempted` is a recorded choice, not a failure, and owes a cause saying what was issued instead.

returned.description: How many items the source gave back under `count_frame`. Null on any non-`reached` status: a count on an unreached cell is a zero laundered out of a failure.

count_frame.description: REQUIRED whenever `returned` is non-zero. What was counted and how — this corpus makes a bare count unre-derivable, because whether an amending act counts separately from the act it amends changes the number without changing the search.

kept.description: How many distinct candidate ROWS this cell carried forward into `candidates` PLUS the `unadmitted` rows naming it — the reading market-competitive, visual, user-research, ml and platform-ecosystem all use. NEVER a result count: under a result-count reading, a row found and dropped WITHOUT a record satisfies the arithmetic, which is the one thing `unadmitted` exists to make impossible.

cause.description: Required for every non-`reached` status, with OBSERVABLE evidence: an HTTP status, a redirect TARGET, a challenge body, a rate-limit header. 'Could not access' is not a cause. A redirect target matters unusually here — two hosts in this registry answer 200 at a URL that silently discards the query.

fallback_used.description: The fallback actually walked, prefixed `angle:<id>` or `row:<id>`. Every angle names one and every row names one; they differ, and a bare id cannot say which was taken.

sanitization.description: Per-cell sanitization record, written ONLY where this cell's fetch departed from the map's wave-0 posture for the same source — an OVERRIDE, so its absence means the map's posture held and is not a gap. Same shape and enum as the map's: one posture recorded two ways teaches a producer to write whichever the nearest example used.

status.description: `clean` nothing was stripped. `modified` something was stripped, and `cause` says what class. `unavailable` the sanitizer could not run — a real state, not a pass. `not-fetched` the posture came from response headers with no body retrieved.

candidate.description: One INSTRUMENT — a regulation, directive, statute, rule, standard or contractual scheme that a named issuing body published and that resolves.

item_id.description: The canonical identity, prefixed by its id class. Six of the seven prefixes are someone else's grammar, which is why `id_class` is checked rather than assumed. INVENTING A CELEX NUMBER IS THE SINGLE WORST THING THIS TYPE CAN DO.

id_class.description: Must agree with `item_id`'s prefix. Recorded separately so the check is an equality rather than a parse.

found_by.description: The (group_id, source_id) CELL this instrument came out of, written `group/source`. Its evidence must be about THAT group. `kept` on that cell counts these rows plus the `unadmitted` ones naming it, so a cell key that does not resolve makes the arithmetic unclosable.

name.description: The short name a regulator would recognise. NOT the official title — a title is a citation, and it is read from the resolved document at extract time, once.

authority.description: How close to the ISSUING BODY this text is. L-5's four tiers, and it RANKS and DEDUPES only — NEVER a cut. Distinct from `binding_force`, and collapsing the two is a defect: a regulator's guidance is authority tier 2 and binding force `regulator-guidance`; PCI DSS is authority tier 3 and binding force `contractual` — not law, and it binds anyway.

binding_force.description: WHETHER and HOW it binds. Orthogonal to `authority`: the question is not how authoritative the text is, but what happens if you ignore it.

locator.description: A resolvable URL, and the one actually fetched. On an identifier-resolver angle that is the resolver URI, not a rendered page — `evidence_quote` is verbatim FROM the locator, so the two must name the same document.

as_of.description: When the FACT became true — for an instrument, its consolidation date. NULL when the document states none; never defaulted to the fetch date, which would be a fabricated fact about the world.

source_claimed_modified_at.description: The page's claim about ITSELF. A claim, not a fact, recorded here so it can never be promoted into `as_of` by accident.

source_claim_provenance.description: Where the self-claimed date came from. `absent` is recorded explicitly rather than left null-by-omission.

evidence_quote.description: The load-bearing sentence or field value, VERBATIM from the locator. Not a paraphrase: the conditions judge the claim against this text. Where the instrument's text is not retrievable this is the CATALOGUE entry's own words, never a paraphrase of a clause nobody read.

claim.description: What the DOCUMENT says, in your words — never what the system MUST DO. `evidence_quote` is the warrant; where the two disagree, the quote governs. A confidently-worded obligation the text does not carry is this type's worst failure.

text_retrievable.description: Whether the instrument's OWN text can be read. Three source classes in this registry cannot be: ISO texts are paywalled behind a challenge, PCI documents 403 from a separate host, and UK primary law refuses non-JS clients. `paywalled` and `blocked` are legitimate terminal states — 'this binds and its text costs money to read' is a finding an architecture doc needs. NEVER paraphrase a clause you could not read.

in_force_date.description: When it starts binding, where the document states one. Distinct from `as_of`: an instrument can be consolidated today and apply from next year, and an architecture decision turns on the difference.

jurisdiction.description: The territory it binds in, as the document states it.

issuing_body.description: The body that published it. L-7 admits an instrument only when this resolves to a named body.

instrument_type.description: The document's own kind. A directive and a regulation impose obligations differently, and the distinction is the document's, not ours.

finding.description: An ABSENCE that is itself evidence: 'the consolidated text states no retention period'. Recorded here rather than left as an empty field, because a hole reads as an oversight and this reads as a fact.

provenance.description: The external identifiers this instrument carries, each null where it has none.

celex.description: The CELEX number, where the instrument has one. Never minted — only transcribed from the resolved document.

eli.description: The ELI URI, where published. A resolvable URI, and never used as a filename: it contains slashes.

cfr_citation.description: The CFR citation as written (`45 CFR 164`), which is a citation and not a filename-safe id.

standard_number.description: The standards-body number (`ISO/IEC 27001`), citable even where the text is paywalled.

notes.description: Anything about THIS instrument worth carrying that is not a claim about its text — a delegated act to follow, a sibling instrument it amends.

unadmitted_row.description: Instruments found and NOT carried into `candidates`, recorded rather than dropped — a silent drop makes 'we did not look' indistinguishable from 'we looked and rejected it'.

item_id.description: The identity of the instrument that was NOT carried, in whatever form this survey saw it. It may not resolve — that is often precisely why the row is here.

found_by.description: The CELL this came out of, so `kept` can reconcile.

name.description: The short name of the instrument that was not carried.

locator.description: Where it was seen, so the next reader starts from the same place. Null when it was named without a link.

reason_class.description: WHY it was not carried, from a closed set in which NO member is an authority judgement. This is deliberate: L-7 refuses admission on VERIFIABILITY — no resolvable text at a named issuing body, no stated version or date — and authority ranks rather than cuts. A free-prose reason could phrase a verifiability failure as 'low authority' and no keyword scan could tell; an enum can.

reason.description: The prose elaboration of `reason_class`, naming what was actually missing.

schema_version.description: Pins the artifact to this contract.

angle_id.description: The registry angle this output is for. It decides the owed grid, the cap and the ordering.

revision.description: Monotonic. A revise round produces a new revision, never a silent rewrite.

note.description: How the wave was run — the budget walked, the delays applied, the fallbacks taken.

meta.description: Facts about THIS run — which angle, when, which revision, and how the wave was worked.

outcome.description: Which of three things happened, and it decides what else is owed. `ran`: cells, and candidates if anything was admitted. `not_run`: NOTHING — the map's verdict ruled this angle out, and searching anyway inflates the survey with an angle the scope excluded. `vacated`: you STARTED and there was nothing to search; cells and causes are owed, candidates are not.

not_run.description: Required when `outcome` is `not_run`. Names the map verdict being honoured, so a reader can check the angle was ruled out by the protocol rather than skipped by the producer.

map_verdict.description: The map verdict being honoured, quoted, so a reader can check the angle was ruled out by the protocol rather than skipped by the producer.

vacated.description: Required when `outcome` is `vacated`. Why there was nothing to search, distinct from a search that returned nothing.

cause.description: Why there was nothing to search — distinct from a search that ran and returned nothing, which is `ran` with a recorded zero.

coverage.description: One cell per OWED (group, source) pair. The owed set is DERIVED from three terms — the angle's applicable group types select the rows, the angle's OWN sources intersected with the map's ACTIVE sources select the columns. Dropping the second term turns a small grid into a large one and reports a correct artifact as full of holes.

candidates.description: The instruments admitted. Each is one INSTRUMENT, never one requirement: how many requirements it holds is knowable only after the read.

unadmitted.description: Instruments found and NOT carried, each with the class of failure that stopped it. The channel that keeps a silent drop from looking like a search that never happened.

bound.description: The per-angle limit, whether it truncated, and the ordering it truncated by.

cap.description: The REGISTRY's cap for this angle. A run may neither raise its own ceiling nor quietly lower it.

hit.description: Whether the cap TRUNCATED: true when the ordering had more to give and the cap stopped it. It reports what the run observed and nothing wider — false is NOT a claim that the corpus was exhausted.

ordering.description: The rule the truncation selected by, stated so a reader can re-apply it. An outcome restated ('the most important instruments first') cannot be re-applied and so cannot show what was dropped.

dropped_note.description: What fell out, when `hit` is true.

ordering_deviation.description: Set when you did NOT apply the declared ordering, with the reason.

retrieval_summary.description: Duplicates the cells on purpose — a discrepancy is the signal that a failure was laundered into a zero.

status_counts.description: One count per cell status, reconciling with `coverage`. It duplicates the cells on purpose — a discrepancy is the signal a failure was laundered into a zero.

degraded_sources.description: Every source with a cell that is neither `reached` nor `not-attempted`.

notes.description: Cross-group leads found while working this angle. The correct channel for something that belongs to another group — never a candidate row.
